The goal of this vignette is to replicate the analysis of PBC data
performed by [@KomarekKomarkovaJSS14mixAK] using package **clustGLMM**.
This is the list of packages required for the analysis:

```{r packages}
library("mixAK")
library("clustGLMM")
```


## PBC910

We use the dataset from package **mixAK**.

```{r pbc-data}
data("PBC910", package = "mixAK")
data <- PBC910
dim(data)
(n <- length(unique(data$id)))      # number of subjects in the data
```

@KomarekKomarkovaJSS14mixAK used the following analysis:

```{r GLMM-MCMC-from-mixAK}
set.seed(20042007)
mod <- GLMM_MCMC(y = PBC910[, c("lbili", "platelet", "spiders")], 
    dist = c("gaussian", "poisson(log)", "binomial(logit)"), 
    id = PBC910[, "id"],
    x = list(lbili    = "empty", 
             platelet = "empty", 
             spiders  = PBC910[, "month"]),
    z = list(lbili    = PBC910[, "month"], 
             platelet = PBC910[, "month"], 
             spiders  = "empty"),
    random.intercept = rep(TRUE, 3),
    prior.b = list(Kmax = 2), 
    nMCMC = c(burn = 100, keep = 1000, thin = 10, info = 100),
    parallel = FALSE)
mod <- NMixRelabel(mod, type = "stephens", keep.comp.prob = TRUE)
```

```{r coda-mcmc-output}
library("coda")
colnames(mod[[1]]$mixture_b)
name.Eb <- paste("b.Mean.", 1:5, sep = "")
RegrChain1 <- mcmc(with(mod[[1]], 
                        cbind(mixture_b[, name.Eb], alpha, sigma_eps)))
RegrChain2 <- mcmc(with(mod[[2]], 
                        cbind(mixture_b[, name.Eb], alpha, sigma_eps)))
colnames(RegrChain1) <- colnames(RegrChain2) <- 
    c(paste(rep(c("lbili", "platelet", "spiders"), each = 2), 
            ":", rep(c("Intcpt", "Slope"), 3), sep = ""),
      "lbili:res_std_dev")
summary(mcmc.list(RegrChain1, RegrChain2))

ip <- getProfiles(t = "month",
                  y = c("lbili", "platelet", "spiders", "jspiders"),
                  id = "id", data = PBC910)
delta <- 0.3
tpred <- seq(0, 30, by = delta)
fit <- fitted(mod[[1]], x =list("empty", "empty", tpred),
              z =list(tpred, tpred, "empty"),
              glmer = TRUE)
names(fit) <- c("lbili", "platelet", "spiders")


K <- mod[[1]]$prior.b$Kmax
clCOL <- c("darkgreen", "red3")
obsCOL <- "azure3"

layout(autolayout(3))
plotProfiles(ip = ip, data = PBC910, var = "lbili", tvar = "month",
             auto.layout = FALSE, main = "Log(bilirubin)",
             xlab = "Time (months)", ylab = "Log(bilirubin)", col = obsCOL)
for (k in 1:K) lines(tpred, fit[["lbili"]][, k], col = clCOL[k], lwd = 2)
plotProfiles(ip = ip, data = PBC910, var = "platelet", tvar = "month",
             auto.layout = FALSE, main = "Platelet count",
             xlab = "Time (months)", ylab = "Platelet count", col = obsCOL)
for (k in 1:K) lines(tpred, fit[["platelet"]][, k], col = clCOL[k], lwd = 2)
plotProfiles(ip = ip, data = PBC910, var = "jspiders", tvar = "month",
             lines = FALSE, points = TRUE,
             auto.layout = FALSE, main = "Blood vessel malform.",
             xlab = "Time (months)", ylab = "Blood vessel malform. (jittered)",
             bg = obsCOL, col = "grey70")
for (k in 1:K) lines(tpred, fit[["spiders"]][, k], col = clCOL[k], lwd = 2)
```


We try to replicate this analysis using package **clustGLMM**. We prepare the data:

```{r data-transformations}
data$time <- data$month
```

The analysis in the paper used as outcome variables:

* numeric serum bilirubin (on log-scale), 
* count variable platelet, 
* binary indicators of blood vessel malformations in the skin (`spiders`).

We create the `family` argument to declare the type of the considered
outcomes for `clustGLMM` analysis:

```{r family}
family <- c(lbili = "num", platelet = "poi", spiders = "bin")
```

We create `formula` to specify the regression model:

```{r formula}
formula <- list()
for (y in names(family)) {
  formula[[y]] <- list()
  formula[[y]]$fixed <- ~ 1
  formula[[y]]$group <- ~ time 
  formula[[y]]$random <- ~ 1
}

formula$spiders$fixed <- ~ time
formula$spiders$group <- ~ 1
formula$spiders$random <- ~ 1
```

Below we show the summary of the variables considered within this
analysis:

```{r data-summary}
summary(data[, c("time", names(family))])
```

We see that some of the outcome values are missing.  However, for
`clustGLMM` there is no need for to omit the rows from the analysis as
long as the missing values are among modelled outcomes.

Now we examine how does the outcome evolve in time:
```{r plot-pbc-vs-time}
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 0.5))
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "lbili", x = "time", id = "id")
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "platelet", x = "time", id = "id")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "spiders", x = "time", main = "spiders")
```

## Sampling MCMC using `clustGLMM`

Some of the key inputs for `clustGLMM` are already prepared (`family`,
`formula`), but there still some key settings to be discussed.
Non-effects parameters of the model may also be set to be
group-specific.  The default setting is provided by

```{r varying}
(varying <- default_varying(prec_num = TRUE, InvSigma = TRUE))
```

Only precision of the errors of numeric outcomes and ordered
intercepts are considered to be group-specific parameters by default.
We set the precision matrix (`InvSigma`) of the vector of random
intercepts to be group-specific as well, but keep its Wishart prior
scale matrix `InvQ` common to all groups.  Missing outcome values will
be always predicted for the current cluster the individual is assigned
to.

Next, we can choose which parameters are returned.  We make just one
change compared to the default setting and that is to save the
predicted missing values.

```{r save}
save <- default_save(naY = TRUE)
```

For `tuning` we will use settings that and `param` will be kept
without any changes.

```{r tuning}
tuning <- default_tuning(experience = TRUE)
param <- default_param(sparse = FALSE)
# param[["prec_num_shp"]] <- 1
# param[["prec_num_rte"]] <- 0.001
# param$InvV <- 0.00000001
# param[["beta_num_fix_sd"]] <- 10
# param[["beta_num_sd"]] <- 10
# data$platelet <- round(data$platelet / 100)
```

<!-- Since we do not know the number of underlying clusters in advance, we -->
<!-- set the maximal number of clusters `G` to 10.  We also apply -->
We are going to fit the same number of clusters `G = 2`. We also apply
standardization of covariates and outcomes to ensure that priors are
truly non-informative.  We run a couple of randomly initialized chains
for initial 1000 iterations.

```{r clustGLMM-burnin, message = FALSE}
set.seed(123456789)
mcmc_burnin <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = "id", family = family, data = data,
                         G = 2, nchains = 2, iter = 1000, 
                         varying = varying, save = save, tuning = tuning, param = param,
                         standardize = TRUE)
```

The default `plot` output informs us about the evolution of number of
patients within each cluster separately for all chains:

```{r plot-mcmc-burnin}
plot(mcmc_burnin)
```
Apparently the number of patients within each cluster stabilizes in time.
<!-- Apparently the number of non-empty groups is decreasing in time.  -->
<!-- Moreover, it seems to differ between chains:  -->

```{r plot-mcmc-burnin-Gplus, eval = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
plot(mcmc_burnin, "Gplus")
```

The current chains cannot be used for inference.
We continue to sample from initial values set to `mcmc_burnin$last`:

```{r clustGLMM-burnin2, message = FALSE}
mcmc_burnin <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = "id", family = family, data = data,
                         G = 2, nchains = 2, iter = 1000, 
                         inits = mcmc_burnin$last,
                         varying = varying, save = save, tuning = tuning, param = param,
                         standardize = TRUE)
```

We plot the same traceplots for the cluster occupancy numbers to detect
potential changes, which actually occur from time to time:
<!-- And we plot the same plots again to see that one chains prefers the -->
<!-- two-cluster solution while the other still keeps 3 clusters while one -->
<!-- of the clusters is rather sparse. -->

```{r plot-mcmc-burnin2}
plot(mcmc_burnin)
```
```{r plot-mcmc-burnin-clusters}
plot(mcmc_burnin, "beta_num", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = 1)
plot(mcmc_burnin, "beta_num", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = 2)
```

Now we sample next $10\,000$ iterations.

```{r clustGLMM}
set.seed(42)
mcmc <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = "id", family = family, data = data,
                  G = 2, nchains = 2, iter = 10000, 
                  inits = mcmc_burnin$last,
                  varying = varying, save = save, tuning = tuning, param = param, 
                  standardize = TRUE)
# mcmc <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = "id", family = family, data = data,
#                   G = 2, nchains = 2, iter = 10000, 
#                   inits = mcmc$last,
#                   varying = varying, save = save, tuning = tuning, param = param, 
#                   standardize = TRUE)
mcmc <- permute_cluster_labels(mcmc, perm = list(1:2, 2:1))
```

```{r plot-mcmc}
plot(mcmc)
```

```{r plot-mcmc-traceplots}
plot(mcmc, "beta_num")
plot(mcmc, "prec_num")
plot(mcmc, "beta_poi")
plot(mcmc, "beta_bin")
plot(mcmc, "sdSigma")
plot(mcmc, "corSigma")
plot(mcmc, "w")
```


```{r plot-mcmc-clusters-kde-ch-1}
ch <- 1
plot(mcmc, "beta_num", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "beta_poi", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "beta_bin", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "beta_ord", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "c_ord", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "sdSigma", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "corSigma", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "w", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
```

```{r plot-mcmc-clusters-kde-ch-2}
ch <- 2
plot(mcmc, "beta_num", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "beta_poi", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "beta_bin", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "beta_ord", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "c_ord", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "sdSigma", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "corSigma", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
plot(mcmc, "w", "clusters_kerneldensity", chain = ch)
```

```{r post-processing}
mcmc_pp <- post_processing(mcmc)
```

```{r Uclustering}
for(ch in 1:2){
  data[, paste0("Uclustering", ch)] <- mcmc$clustering[as.character(data$id), ch]
}
```

```{r plot-pbc-vs-time-clustered-ch-1, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8}
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 0.5))
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "lbili", x = "time", group = "Uclustering1", id = "id")
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "platelet", x = "time", group = "Uclustering1", id = "id")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "spiders", x = "time", group = "Uclustering1", main = "spiders")
```
```{r plot-pbc-vs-time-clustered-ch-2, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8}
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 0.5))
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "lbili", x = "time", group = "Uclustering2", id = "id")
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "platelet", x = "time", group = "Uclustering2", id = "id")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, y = "spiders", x = "time", group = "Uclustering2", main = "spiders")
```
